title: Search observable surfaces first, then broaden to closed containers
principle: When the target object's location is unknown, locate it before manipulation by checking open, directly observable surfaces and common holding places first: tables, countertops, desks, dressers, shelves, beds, sofas, chairs, and other plausible visible surfaces such as toilets or TV stands when they could hold the target. Only then open closed containers such as drawers, cabinets, fridges, microwaves, and similar receptacles. Treat search as a broad multi-location search rather than assuming one named receptacle contains the object. If an early location is empty, broaden to other plausible unchecked locations. If the target or a required fixture is already visible on a surface, go directly to that furniture instead of continuing unrelated container checks.
when_to_apply: When the target object's location is unknown at the start, when the first checked location does not contain it, or when the target or a required fixture is already visible on a surface.
[General | G_002 | Failure Lesson]
description: Failed searches often repeat the same empty surfaces or failed take attempts, revisit already-confirmed-empty locations, or conclude the object is unavailable before all plausible open surfaces and relevant containers have been checked. A search should maintain a checked-location list and move to a new unchecked plausible location after a failed take or empty look.
why_it_happens: Search may be treated as an unconstrained sequence without bookkeeping, so empty locations are revisited and some plausible locations are never examined; alternatively, failure may be declared after only a subset of locations is checked.
how_to_avoid: Record each checked location and its result. After a failed take or empty look, mark that location checked and move to another plausible unchecked location. Do not revisit confirmed empty surfaces unless the environment state changed. Open closed receptacles before treating them as searched and prioritize locations by object type. If the object remains absent after relevant locations are exhausted, report failure rather than continuing indefinitely; but do not declare blocked while plausible unchecked locations remain.
[General | G_003 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Open closed containers before taking or placing and verify destination openability
principle: When a closed drawer, cabinet, safe, fridge, microwave, or similar container may hold the target or is the placement destination, navigate to it and open it before attempting to take from it or put into it. Closed containers cannot be inspected or used directly. Before placing, confirm the destination is already open or can be opened; if opening returns no change, treat it as non-openable and choose a valid open destination or surface. For non-openable fixtures, use only a go-then-put sequence.
when_to_apply: When the target may be inside a closed container, or when the placement destination is closed or its openability is uncertain.
[General | G_004 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Position at the object's receptacle before take and at the destination before put
principle: A take action succeeds only when the actor is at the receptacle where the object is present, and a put action succeeds only when the actor is at the destination. When retrieving, first locate the object and position at its receptacle before taking. Once the target is held, travel directly to the specified destination and place it without unnecessary intermediate steps; if a put fails, verify current location and navigate to the destination before retrying.
when_to_apply: When retrieving an object whose location is not current, when moving a held object to a destination, or after a failed put.
[General | G_005 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Use supported action forms, exact identifiers, and matching object instances
principle: Use only supported action forms: go to a location, take an object from a receptacle, put an object in or on a receptacle, open a container before accessing it, and use a fixture with its numbered instance when applicable. Refer to exact object and receptacle identifiers from observations, including instance numbers, and track the specific instance taken so later actions use the same one. Prefer navigating to locations, furniture, or receptacles rather than to a takeable object when the action form requires it. Do not use examine, look at, or open on non-container surfaces; open only applies to openable containers. Before taking or transforming, confirm the object name matches the goal, because similar types may not satisfy it. If many containers have been checked without success, reassess visible surfaces and the target description rather than continuing blind exhaustive checks.
when_to_apply: Throughout object search, retrieval, and placement, especially when forming commands or when an action seems unsupported or ambiguous.
[General | G_006 | Failure Lesson]
description: When an action such as go to, open, take, put, use, or clean returns no change, do not repeat the same command. Failed attempts can come from being at the wrong location, using an inexact or invalid identifier, targeting a closed or non-openable receptacle, or trying an inaccessible location. Treat an unreachable navigation target as unavailable and switch to another candidate; treat an already-open container as open and continue rather than reopening it. Repeated no-change results are evidence that the current approach is exhausted.
why_it_happens: The same invalid action may be retried without updating the inferred state, and a failed task segment may be reissued identically instead of changing the search location, object description, or strategy.
how_to_avoid: After a no-change observation, re-check location, inventory, exact identifiers, and object or container state. Change at least one relevant condition: move to a different reachable location, open a closed container, use the specific instance id, or switch to another strategy. After one or two identical failures, stop retrying. If a task segment fails or returns without meeting its condition, do not repeat it unchanged; broaden the search or change the approach. Before declaring blocked, ensure every plausible closed container was actually opened and inspected, not merely approached, and avoid revisiting surfaces already confirmed empty.
[General | G_007 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Separate acquisition from operation with observable completion conditions
principle: For tasks that require an object to be found and then manipulated, cleaned, heated, cooled, examined, or placed, split the task into an acquisition phase and an operation phase. The acquisition phase ends only when the target object is actually held, not merely seen and not merely because a container was opened. The operation phase ends only when the environment observation confirms the required final state, such as the object being at the destination, cleaned, heated, or cooled. Begin placement only after acquisition is confirmed by holding the target object. If a subsequent phase or handoff follows, report acquisition only after the take observation confirms holding and note any remaining operation.
when_to_apply: When a goal requires an object to be acquired before it is used, transformed, or placed, and the object is not already held.
[General | G_008 | Failure Lesson]
description: Do not declare completion or stop based on an attempted action alone. After critical actions such as take, put, clean, heat, or cool, inspect the observation for the goal predicate. Declare success only when the observation confirms the required final state; declare failure only when the observation shows an invalid or blocked action, an unreachable object, or exhaustion of plausible locations. If the placement observation already confirms the goal, treat it as terminal and do not run a redundant verification step.
why_it_happens: An action may be assumed successful without checking feedback, failure may be declared after a successful sequence, or an unnecessary verification step may be added after success, causing loops.
how_to_avoid: After each critical action, compare the observation with the expected state. If the action failed, retry only after adjusting the approach; if it succeeded, stop issuing extra actions. Treat a confirming placement, cleaning, heating, or cooling observation as the terminal success condition. Do not declare completion before the final placement is confirmed; after confirmation, stop and do not send empty or inventory-only actions.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_001 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Two-item sequential placement with per-item verification and placed-item tracking
principle: Treat a two-item placement goal as two search-and-place cycles. For each cycle: locate and take one target object, navigate to the destination, open it if closed, place the object, and verify the placement from the observation before starting the next cycle. Track how many items are placed and which item was already placed; never take an already-placed item again. If a second take fails while an object is held, place the held object at the destination before returning for the second. If both instances are visible on the same surface or receptacle, place the first and then return to that same location for the second. If the final destination is temporarily unavailable, use only a safe recoverable holding location when necessary, then move both objects to the final destination afterward. Treat each placement as a checkpoint, not task completion.
when_to_apply: When the goal requires placing two instances of the same object type at one target location and only one object can be carried at a time.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_002 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Systematic broad search with checked-location tracking
principle: When target objects are not immediately visible, search broadly rather than checking only one receptacle type. Inspect visible open surfaces such as counters, tables, shelves, sofas, and similar surfaces first, then check closed containers such as cabinets and drawers, opening them before inspecting or taking from inside. Continue across multiple location types until the required number of instances is found or a checked-location record shows no remaining unchecked likely locations. If both target instances are visible on the same surface, take one, place it, then return to that same surface for the second rather than wandering to unrelated containers. Treat an unreachable or no-change navigation target as unavailable and move to another candidate. Reassess feasibility after likely locations are exhausted, but do not conclude the task is blocked prematurely.
when_to_apply: When one or both target objects are not visible and must be located in the environment.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_003 | Failure Lesson]
description: Attempts to take a second object, or sometimes to move to another location, while already holding an object can return no effect. This blocks progress in two-item placement if the held object is not released first. A failed second take while an object is held should be diagnosed as the one-item carry limit, not as the second object being absent.
why_it_happens: The environment commonly allows carrying only one object at a time, so take or movement actions may be rejected while inventory is occupied.
how_to_avoid: Before taking the second object or moving to search elsewhere, put the held object into the final destination or into a safe recoverable temporary location. Confirm the hands are empty, then continue. When a take fails while holding an object, attribute it to occupied inventory and place the held object first rather than concluding the target is missing.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_004 | Failure Lesson]
description: A put action can produce no effect if issued before reaching the destination receptacle, or it can fail without the failure being noticed. Continuing to search for the second item after an unconfirmed first placement can leave the goal unsatisfied. When a put returns no change, first verify that the actor is actually at the destination before concluding the receptacle rejects placement. If the destination repeatedly rejects placement after the location cause is ruled out, reassess whether it is valid and report blocked rather than looping or abandoning the held object.
why_it_happens: Placement requires being at the target container, and a successful put must be verified from the observation; otherwise the first item may still be held or not placed. Misattributing a location failure to receptacle type can lead to wrong alternative-destination actions, while some named destinations may be invalid or unreachable.
how_to_avoid: Navigate to the destination before placing. After each put, inspect the observation to confirm success. If the put did not succeed, verify the current location, move to the target if needed, and retry before starting the next search or placement cycle. Do not switch to an alternative receptacle until the destination-location cause has been ruled out; if repeated rejection continues, reassess validity and report blocked.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_005 | Failure Lesson]
description: Attempting to put an object into, or take an object from, a closed cabinet, drawer, or similar container may produce no effect. Issuing open on an already-open container may also return no change and should not be retried. Issuing open on a container while standing at its parent furniture may return no change; the actor must navigate to the container itself first.
why_it_happens: The environment requires the container to be open before its contents can be accessed or modified, reports no change when opening an already-open container, and validates open actions against the actor's current location being the container rather than its parent furniture.
how_to_avoid: Navigate to the container itself, then open it with the appropriate open action. If it is already open, or if opening returns no change, proceed to take or place rather than retrying open. After opening, verify access before taking or placing. Do not issue open on a container from its parent furniture.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_006 | Failure Lesson]
description: Using an examine-style action on objects or locations is not supported and returns no useful information.
why_it_happens: The available interaction set is limited to navigation, taking, putting, opening, and inventory-style operations; examining is not an effective substitute.
how_to_avoid: Inspect a location by navigating to the receptacle and observing its contents. Pick up visible target objects with a take action from that receptacle.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_007 | Failure Lesson]
description: Placing an object into a non-target or unsuitable container such as a garbage can can make retrieval impossible or cause the overall two-item placement to fail.
why_it_happens: Some containers may not accept objects cleanly, may change object state, or may not allow reliable retrieval; temporary storage is only safe if the object can be taken back.
how_to_avoid: Prefer placing the first object directly into the final destination. If temporary holding is unavoidable, choose an open, stable, recoverable surface or container and avoid garbage cans or other likely irreversible containers.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_008 | Failure Lesson]
description: After several containers have been opened and no target found, repeatedly revisiting locations already confirmed empty, re-taking an already-placed instance, repeating a no-change navigation, or trying yet another receptacle after many failed put attempts can exhaust the action budget and cause failure. A held object whose put attempts fail across many receptacles may indicate an unplaceable object or an infeasible goal rather than a wrong receptacle.
why_it_happens: Searching without tracking checked locations and placed instances leads to redundant actions, while unchecked opened containers or visible surfaces may still contain the target. A no-change navigation indicates the target location is unreachable or invalid, so retrying it cannot help.
how_to_avoid: Maintain a list of checked locations and placed instances. Prioritize unchecked opened containers and visible surfaces; take a target directly if it is visible. Avoid revisiting a location confirmed to have no target or re-taking an already-placed object unless new evidence suggests otherwise. After one no-change navigation, choose a different unchecked location. If every put attempt fails across many receptacles, stop suggesting new receptacles and reassess the held object's exact identifier and whether the destination accepts placement, considering the object unplaceable or the goal infeasible.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_009 | Failure Lesson]
description: Repeatedly declaring a subtask complete without executing the required next action can trigger a loop guard and terminate the episode before the two items are placed. Re-taking an already-placed item and re-placing it at a different instance of the destination can also trigger a guard.
why_it_happens: The current state may be misread as satisfying the completion condition even though the actual goal or subgoal is unfinished, causing repeated signals instead of progress; alternatively, the destination instance may be confused, leading to re-taking a placed item.
how_to_avoid: Signal completion only after the corresponding subgoal is actually achieved, such as an object being taken or placed. After signaling, continue with the necessary next action and avoid repeating the same completion signal without new progress. Track which destination instance is the goal; once an item is placed at the target, do not re-take it—search for a second instance instead.

You are an executor in a household text environment.
The OVERALL TASK is supplied only as context. Solve only the CURRENT SUBTASK
supplied by the controller; do not infer or attempt later planned subtasks.
The CURRENT SUBTASK has completion priority: as soon as its required end state
is satisfied, immediately return Status: COMPLETED. Do not continue acting to
complete the overall task or any later planned subtask after that point.

For every nonterminal turn, return exactly two lines:
Thought: one short sentence about the next action for the current subtask.
Action: one environment command.

When the CURRENT SUBTASK has been completed, return exactly:
Thought: one short completion reason.
Status: COMPLETED

Do not declare FAILED after one invalid action or one unsuccessful search.
Only after sufficiently attempting the CURRENT SUBTASK with valid environment
interactions may you return exactly:
Thought: brief concrete evidence of the valid attempts already made.
Status: FAILED

Never include an Action line and a Status line in the same response. An Action
has not succeeded until the environment returns an observation. Therefore, use
Status: COMPLETED only in a later response after observing that the preceding
single Action completed the CURRENT SUBTASK.

If the environment says 'Nothing happens.', the preceding Action was invalid
and did not change the environment state. Choose a different Action; do not
repeat that failed Action unless the state has changed.

Use names exactly as present in the observation. The accepted command forms are:
go to <receptacle>
open <receptacle>
close <receptacle>
take <object> from <receptacle>
put <object> in/on <receptacle> (type the literal token "in/on")
use <object>
clean <object> with <sink or bathtub>
heat <object> with <microwave>
cool <object> with <fridge>
inventory
look
examine <object or receptacle>

Do not output a plan, an explanation, or commands outside this grammar.

ALFWORLD OPERATION CARD:
- Carry only one object. Before take or put, go to the object's or destination
  receptacle; open it first if it is closed.
- Cleaning, heating, and cooling depend on the held object and current
  environment state. Do not assume an object must first be placed inside an appliance.
- A desklamp is fixed and cannot be taken.
- 'Nothing happens.' means the preceding Action was invalid and changed no
  state. Choose a different Action unless state has changed.

[General | G_001 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Search observable surfaces first, then broaden to closed containers
principle: When the target object's location is unknown, locate it before manipulation by checking open, directly observable surfaces and common holding places first: tables, countertops, desks, dressers, shelves, beds, sofas, chairs, and other plausible visible surfaces such as toilets or TV stands when they could hold the target. Only then open closed containers such as drawers, cabinets, fridges, microwaves, and similar receptacles. Treat search as a broad multi-location search rather than assuming one named receptacle contains the object. If an early location is empty, broaden to other plausible unchecked locations. If the target or a required fixture is already visible on a surface, go directly to that furniture instead of continuing unrelated container checks.
when_to_apply: When the target object's location is unknown at the start, when the first checked location does not contain it, or when the target or a required fixture is already visible on a surface.
[General | G_002 | Failure Lesson]
description: Failed searches often repeat the same empty surfaces or failed take attempts, revisit already-confirmed-empty locations, or conclude the object is unavailable before all plausible open surfaces and relevant containers have been checked. A search should maintain a checked-location list and move to a new unchecked plausible location after a failed take or empty look.
why_it_happens: Search may be treated as an unconstrained sequence without bookkeeping, so empty locations are revisited and some plausible locations are never examined; alternatively, failure may be declared after only a subset of locations is checked.
how_to_avoid: Record each checked location and its result. After a failed take or empty look, mark that location checked and move to another plausible unchecked location. Do not revisit confirmed empty surfaces unless the environment state changed. Open closed receptacles before treating them as searched and prioritize locations by object type. If the object remains absent after relevant locations are exhausted, report failure rather than continuing indefinitely; but do not declare blocked while plausible unchecked locations remain.
[General | G_003 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Open closed containers before taking or placing and verify destination openability
principle: When a closed drawer, cabinet, safe, fridge, microwave, or similar container may hold the target or is the placement destination, navigate to it and open it before attempting to take from it or put into it. Closed containers cannot be inspected or used directly. Before placing, confirm the destination is already open or can be opened; if opening returns no change, treat it as non-openable and choose a valid open destination or surface. For non-openable fixtures, use only a go-then-put sequence.
when_to_apply: When the target may be inside a closed container, or when the placement destination is closed or its openability is uncertain.
[General | G_004 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Position at the object's receptacle before take and at the destination before put
principle: A take action succeeds only when the actor is at the receptacle where the object is present, and a put action succeeds only when the actor is at the destination. When retrieving, first locate the object and position at its receptacle before taking. Once the target is held, travel directly to the specified destination and place it without unnecessary intermediate steps; if a put fails, verify current location and navigate to the destination before retrying.
when_to_apply: When retrieving an object whose location is not current, when moving a held object to a destination, or after a failed put.
[General | G_005 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Use supported action forms, exact identifiers, and matching object instances
principle: Use only supported action forms: go to a location, take an object from a receptacle, put an object in or on a receptacle, open a container before accessing it, and use a fixture with its numbered instance when applicable. Refer to exact object and receptacle identifiers from observations, including instance numbers, and track the specific instance taken so later actions use the same one. Prefer navigating to locations, furniture, or receptacles rather than to a takeable object when the action form requires it. Do not use examine, look at, or open on non-container surfaces; open only applies to openable containers. Before taking or transforming, confirm the object name matches the goal, because similar types may not satisfy it. If many containers have been checked without success, reassess visible surfaces and the target description rather than continuing blind exhaustive checks.
when_to_apply: Throughout object search, retrieval, and placement, especially when forming commands or when an action seems unsupported or ambiguous.
[General | G_006 | Failure Lesson]
description: When an action such as go to, open, take, put, use, or clean returns no change, do not repeat the same command. Failed attempts can come from being at the wrong location, using an inexact or invalid identifier, targeting a closed or non-openable receptacle, or trying an inaccessible location. Treat an unreachable navigation target as unavailable and switch to another candidate; treat an already-open container as open and continue rather than reopening it. Repeated no-change results are evidence that the current approach is exhausted.
why_it_happens: The same invalid action may be retried without updating the inferred state, and a failed task segment may be reissued identically instead of changing the search location, object description, or strategy.
how_to_avoid: After a no-change observation, re-check location, inventory, exact identifiers, and object or container state. Change at least one relevant condition: move to a different reachable location, open a closed container, use the specific instance id, or switch to another strategy. After one or two identical failures, stop retrying. If a task segment fails or returns without meeting its condition, do not repeat it unchanged; broaden the search or change the approach. Before declaring blocked, ensure every plausible closed container was actually opened and inspected, not merely approached, and avoid revisiting surfaces already confirmed empty.
[General | G_007 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Separate acquisition from operation with observable completion conditions
principle: For tasks that require an object to be found and then manipulated, cleaned, heated, cooled, examined, or placed, split the task into an acquisition phase and an operation phase. The acquisition phase ends only when the target object is actually held, not merely seen and not merely because a container was opened. The operation phase ends only when the environment observation confirms the required final state, such as the object being at the destination, cleaned, heated, or cooled. Begin placement only after acquisition is confirmed by holding the target object. If a subsequent phase or handoff follows, report acquisition only after the take observation confirms holding and note any remaining operation.
when_to_apply: When a goal requires an object to be acquired before it is used, transformed, or placed, and the object is not already held.

description: Do not declare completion or stop based on an attempted action alone. After critical actions such as take, put, clean, heat, or cool, inspect the observation for the goal predicate. 当前可用 skill：
[General | G_001 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Search observable surfaces first, then broaden to closed containers
principle: When the target object's location is unknown, locate it before manipulation by checking open, directly observable surfaces and common holding places first: tables, countertops, desks, dressers, shelves, beds, sofas, chairs, and other plausible visible surfaces such as toilets or TV stands when they could hold the target. Only then open closed containers such as drawers, cabinets, fridges, microwaves, and similar receptacles. Treat search as a broad multi-location search rather than assuming one named receptacle contains the object. If an early location is empty, broaden to other plausible unchecked locations. If the target or a required fixture is already visible on a surface, go directly to that furniture instead of continuing unrelated container checks.
when_to_apply: When the target object's location is unknown at the start, when the first checked location does not contain it, or when the target or a required fixture is already visible on a surface.
[General | G_002 | Failure Lesson]
description: Failed searches often repeat the same empty surfaces or failed take attempts, revisit already-confirmed-empty locations, or conclude the object is unavailable before all plausible open surfaces and relevant containers have been checked. A search should maintain a checked-location list and move to a new unchecked plausible location after a failed take or empty look.
why_it_happens: Search may be treated as an unconstrained sequence without bookkeeping, so empty locations are revisited and some plausible locations are never examined; alternatively, failure may be declared after only a subset of locations is checked.
how_to_avoid: Record each checked location and its result. After a failed take or empty look, mark that location checked and move to another plausible unchecked location. Do not revisit confirmed empty surfaces unless the environment state changed. Open closed receptacles before treating them as searched and prioritize locations by object type. If the object remains absent after relevant locations are exhausted, report failure rather than continuing indefinitely; but do not declare blocked while plausible unchecked locations remain.
[General | G_003 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Open closed containers before taking or placing and verify destination openability
principle: When a closed drawer, cabinet, safe, fridge, microwave, or similar container may hold the target or is the placement destination, navigate to it and open it before attempting to take from it or put into it. Closed containers cannot be inspected or used directly. Before placing, confirm the destination is already open or can be opened; if opening returns no change, treat it as non-openable and choose a valid open destination or surface. For non-openable fixtures, use only a go-then-put sequence.
when_to_apply: When the target may be inside a closed container, or when the placement destination is closed or its openability is uncertain.
[General | G_004 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Position at the object's receptacle before take and at the destination before put
principle: A take action succeeds only when the actor is at the receptacle where the object is present, and a put action succeeds only when the actor is at the destination. When retrieving, first locate the object and position at its receptacle before taking. Once the target is held, travel directly to the specified destination and place it without unnecessary intermediate steps; if a put fails, verify current location and navigate to the destination before retrying.
when_to_apply: When retrieving an object whose location is not current, when moving a held object to a destination, or after a failed put.
[General | G_005 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Use supported action forms, exact identifiers, and matching object instances
principle: Use only supported action forms: go to a location, take an object from a receptacle, put an object in or on a receptacle, open a container before accessing it, and use a fixture with its numbered instance when applicable. Refer to exact object and receptacle identifiers from observations, including instance numbers, and track the specific instance taken so later actions use the same one. Prefer navigating to locations, furniture, or receptacles rather than to a takeable object when the action form requires it. Do not use examine, look at, or open on non-container surfaces; open only applies to openable containers. Before taking or transforming, confirm the object name matches the goal, because similar types may not satisfy it. If many containers have been checked without success, reassess visible surfaces and the target description rather than continuing blind exhaustive checks.
when_to_apply: Throughout object search, retrieval, and placement, especially when forming commands or when an action seems unsupported or ambiguous.
[General | G_006 | Failure Lesson]
description: When an action such as go to, open, take, put, use, or clean returns no change, do not repeat the same command. Failed attempts can come from being at the wrong location, using an inexact or invalid identifier, targeting a closed or non-openable receptacle, or trying an inaccessible location. Treat an unreachable navigation target as unavailable and switch to another candidate; treat an already-open container as open and continue rather than reopening it. Repeated no-change results are evidence that the current approach is exhausted.
why_it_happens: The same invalid action may be retried without updating the inferred state, and a failed task segment may be reissued identically instead of changing the search location, object description, or strategy.
how_to_avoid: After a no-change observation, re-check location, inventory, exact identifiers, and object or container state. Change at least one relevant condition: move to a different reachable location, open a closed container, use the specific instance id, or switch to another strategy. After one or two identical failures, stop retrying. If a task segment fails or returns without meeting its condition, do not repeat it unchanged; broaden the search or change the approach. Before declaring blocked, ensure every plausible closed container was actually opened and inspected, not merely approached, and avoid revisiting surfaces already confirmed empty.
[General | G_007 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Separate acquisition from operation with observable completion conditions
principle: For tasks that require an object to be found and then manipulated, cleaned, heated, cooled, examined, or placed, split the task into an acquisition phase and an operation phase. The acquisition phase ends only when the target object is actually held, not merely seen and not merely because a container was opened. The operation phase ends only when the environment observation confirms the required final state, such as the object being at the destination, cleaned, heated, or cooled. Begin placement only after acquisition is confirmed by holding the target object. If a subsequent phase or handoff follows, report acquisition only after the take observation confirms holding and note any remaining operation.
when_to_apply: When a goal requires an object to be acquired before it is used, transformed, or placed, and the object is not already held.
[General | G_008 | Failure Lesson]
description: Do not declare completion or stop based on an attempted action alone. After critical actions such as take, put, clean, heat, or cool, inspect the observation for the goal predicate. Declare success only when the observation confirms the required final state; declare failure only when the observation shows an invalid or blocked action, an unreachable object, or exhaustion of plausible locations. If the placement observation already confirms the goal, treat it as terminal and do not run a redundant verification step.
why_it_happens: An action may be assumed successful without checking feedback, failure may be declared after a successful sequence, or an unnecessary verification step may be added after success, causing loops.
how_to_avoid: After each critical action, compare the observation with the expected state. If the action failed, retry only after adjusting the approach; if it succeeded, stop issuing extra actions. Treat a confirming placement, cleaning, heating, or cooling observation as the terminal success condition. Do not declare completion before the final placement is confirmed; after confirmation, stop and do not send empty or inventory-only actions.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_001 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Two-item sequential placement with per-item verification and placed-item tracking
principle: Treat a two-item placement goal as two search-and-place cycles. For each cycle: locate and take one target object, navigate to the destination, open it if closed, place the object, and verify the placement from the observation before starting the next cycle. Track how many items are placed and which item was already placed; never take an already-placed item again. If a second take fails while an object is held, place the held object at the destination before returning for the second. If both instances are visible on the same surface or receptacle, place the first and then return to that same location for the second. If the final destination is temporarily unavailable, use only a safe recoverable holding location when necessary, then move both objects to the final destination afterward. Treat each placement as a checkpoint, not task completion.
when_to_apply: When the goal requires placing two instances of the same object type at one target location and only one object can be carried at a time.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_002 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Systematic broad search with checked-location tracking
principle: When target objects are not immediately visible, search broadly rather than checking only one receptacle type. Inspect visible open surfaces such as counters, tables, shelves, sofas, and similar surfaces first, then check closed containers such as cabinets and drawers, opening them before inspecting or taking from inside. Continue across multiple location types until the required number of instances is found or a checked-location record shows no remaining unchecked likely locations. If both target instances are visible on the same surface, take one, place it, then return to that same surface for the second rather than wandering to unrelated containers. Treat an unreachable or no-change navigation target as unavailable and move to another candidate. Reassess feasibility after likely locations are exhausted, but do not conclude the task is blocked prematurely.
when_to_apply: When one or both target objects are not visible and must be located in the environment.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_003 | Failure Lesson]
description: Attempts to take a second object, or sometimes to move to another location, while already holding an object can return no effect. This blocks progress in two-item placement if the held object is not released first. A failed second take while an object is held should be diagnosed as the one-item carry limit, not as the second object being absent.
why_it_happens: The environment commonly allows carrying only one object at a time, so take or movement actions may be rejected while inventory is occupied.
how_to_avoid: Before taking the second object or moving to search elsewhere, put the held object into the final destination or into a safe recoverable temporary location. Confirm the hands are empty, then continue. When a take fails while holding an object, attribute it to occupied inventory and place the held object first rather than concluding the target is missing.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_004 | Failure Lesson]
description: A put action can produce no effect if issued before reaching the destination receptacle, or it can fail without the failure being noticed. Continuing to search for the second item after an unconfirmed first placement can leave the goal unsatisfied. When a put returns no change, first verify that the actor is actually at the destination before concluding the receptacle rejects placement. If the destination repeatedly rejects placement after the location cause is ruled out, reassess whether it is valid and report blocked rather than looping or abandoning the held object.
why_it_happens: Placement requires being at the target container, and a successful put must be verified from the observation; otherwise the first item may still be held or not placed. Misattributing a location failure to receptacle type can lead to wrong alternative-destination actions, while some named destinations may be invalid or unreachable.
how_to_avoid: Navigate to the destination before placing. After each put, inspect the observation to confirm success. If the put did not succeed, verify the current location, move to the target if needed, and retry before starting the next search or placement cycle. Do not switch to an alternative receptacle until the destination-location cause has been ruled out; if repeated rejection continues, reassess validity and report blocked.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_005 | Failure Lesson]
description: Attempting to put an object into, or take an object from, a closed cabinet, drawer, or similar container may produce no effect. Issuing open on an already-open container may also return no change and should not be retried. Issuing open on a container while standing at its parent furniture may return no change; the actor must navigate to the container itself first.
why_it_happens: The environment requires the container to be open before its contents can be accessed or modified, reports no change when opening an already-open container, and validates open actions against the actor's current location being the container rather than its parent furniture.
how_to_avoid: Navigate to the container itself, then open it with the appropriate open action. If it is already open, or if opening returns no change, proceed to take or place rather than retrying open. After opening, verify access before taking or placing. Do not issue open on a container from its parent furniture.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_006 | Failure Lesson]
description: Using an examine-style action on objects or locations is not supported and returns no useful information.
why_it_happens: The available interaction set is limited to navigation, taking, putting, opening, and inventory-style operations; examining is not an effective substitute.
how_to_avoid: Inspect a location by navigating to the receptacle and observing its contents. Pick up visible target objects with a take action from that receptacle.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_007 | Failure Lesson]
description: Placing an object into a non-target or unsuitable container such as a garbage can can make retrieval impossible or cause the overall two-item placement to fail.
why_it_happens: Some containers may not accept objects cleanly, may change object state, or may not allow reliable retrieval; temporary storage is only safe if the object can be taken back.
how_to_avoid: Prefer placing the first object directly into the final destination. If temporary holding is unavoidable, choose an open, stable, recoverable surface or container and avoid garbage cans or other likely irreversible containers.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_008 | Failure Lesson]
description: After several containers have been opened and no target found, repeatedly revisiting locations already confirmed empty, re-taking an already-placed instance, repeating a no-change navigation, or trying yet another receptacle after many failed put attempts can exhaust the action budget and cause failure. A held object whose put attempts fail across many receptacles may indicate an unplaceable object or an infeasible goal rather than a wrong receptacle.
why_it_happens: Searching without tracking checked locations and placed instances leads to redundant actions, while unchecked opened containers or visible surfaces may still contain the target. A no-change navigation indicates the target location is unreachable or invalid, so retrying it cannot help.
how_to_avoid: Maintain a list of checked locations and placed instances. Prioritize unchecked opened containers and visible surfaces; take a target directly if it is visible. Avoid revisiting a location confirmed to have no target or re-taking an already-placed object unless new evidence suggests otherwise. After one no-change navigation, choose a different unchecked location. If every put attempt fails across many receptacles, stop suggesting new receptacles and reassess the held object's exact identifier and whether the destination accepts placement, considering the object unplaceable or the goal infeasible.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_009 | Failure Lesson]
description: Repeatedly declaring a subtask complete without executing the required next action can trigger a loop guard and terminate the episode before the two items are placed. Re-taking an already-placed item and re-placing it at a different instance of the destination can also trigger a guard.
why_it_happens: The current state may be misread as satisfying the completion condition even though the actual goal or subgoal is unfinished, causing repeated signals instead of progress; alternatively, the destination instance may be confused, leading to re-taking a placed item.
how_to_avoid: Signal completion only after the corresponding subgoal is actually achieved, such as an object being taken or placed. After signaling, continue with the necessary next action and avoid repeating the same completion signal without new progress. Track which destination instance is the goal; once an item is placed at the target, do not re-take it—search for a second instance instead.

find two cellphone and put them in dresser.

Find and take the second cellphone.

CONTROLLER HANDOFF (factual state, not a trajectory):

put cellphone 3 in/on dresser 1

request_messages.content:
You are an executor in a household text environment.
The OVERALL TASK is supplied only as context. Solve only the CURRENT SUBTASK
supplied by the controller; do not infer or attempt later planned subtasks.
The CURRENT SUBTASK has completion priority: as soon as its required end state
is satisfied, immediately return Status: COMPLETED. Do not continue acting to
complete the overall task or any later planned subtask after that point.

For every nonterminal turn, return exactly two lines:
Thought: one short sentence about the next action for the current subtask.
Action: one environment command.

When the CURRENT SUBTASK has been completed, return exactly:
Thought: one short completion reason.
Status: COMPLETED

Do not declare FAILED after one invalid action or one unsuccessful search.
Only after sufficiently attempting the CURRENT SUBTASK with valid environment
interactions may you return exactly:
Thought: brief concrete evidence of the valid attempts already made.
Status: FAILED

Never include an Action line and a Status line in the same response. An Action
has not succeeded until the environment returns an observation. Therefore, use
Status: COMPLETED only in a later response after observing that the preceding
single Action completed the CURRENT SUBTASK.

If the environment says 'Nothing happens.', the preceding Action was invalid
and did not change the environment state. Choose a different Action; do not
repeat that failed Action unless the state has changed.

Use names exactly as present in the observation. The accepted command forms are:
go to <receptacle>
open <receptacle>
close <receptacle>
take <object> from <receptacle>
put <object> in/on <receptacle> (type the literal token "in/on")
use <object>
clean <object> with <sink or bathtub>
heat <object> with <microwave>
cool <object> with <fridge>
inventory
look
examine <object or receptacle>

Do not output a plan, an explanation, or commands outside this grammar.

ALFWORLD OPERATION CARD:
- Carry only one object. Before take or put, go to the object's or destination
  receptacle; open it first if it is closed.
- Cleaning, heating, and cooling depend on the held object and current
  environment state. Do not assume an object must first be placed inside an appliance.
- A desklamp is fixed and cannot be taken.
- 'Nothing happens.' means the preceding Action was invalid and changed no
  state. Choose a different Action unless state has changed.

when_to_apply: When the goal requires placing two instances of the same object type at one target location and only one object can be carried at a time.

when_to_apply: When one or both target objects are not visible and must be located in the environment.

[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_004 | Failure Lesson]

[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_005 | Failure Lesson]
description: Attempting to put an object into, or take an object from, a closed cabinet, drawer, or similar container may produce no effect. Issuing open on a container while standing at its parent furniture may return no change; the actor must navigate to the container itself first.
why_it_happens: The environment requires the container to be open before its contents can be accessed or modified, reports no change when opening an already-open container, and validates open actions against the actor's current location being the container rather than its parent furniture.
how_to_avoid: Navigate to the container itself, then open it with the appropriate open action. If it is already open, or if opening returns no change, proceed to take or place rather than retrying open. After opening, verify access before taking or placing. Do not issue open on a container from its parent furniture.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_006 | Failure Lesson]
description: Using an examine-style action on objects or locations is not supported and returns no useful information.
why_it_happens: The available interaction set is limited to navigation, taking, putting, opening, and inventory-style operations; examining is not an effective substitute.
how_to_avoid: Inspect a location by navigating to the receptacle and observing its contents. Pick up visible target objects with a take action from that receptacle.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_007 | Failure Lesson]
description: Placing an object into a non-target or unsuitable container such as a garbage can can make retrieval impossible or cause the overall two-item placement to fail.
why_it_happens: Some containers may not accept objects cleanly, may change object state, or may not allow reliable retrieval; temporary storage is only safe if the object can be taken back.
how_to_avoid: Prefer placing the first object directly into the final destination. If temporary holding is unavoidable, choose an open, stable, recoverable surface or container and avoid garbage cans or other likely irreversible containers.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_008 | Failure Lesson]
description: After several containers have been opened and no target found, repeatedly revisiting locations already confirmed empty, re-taking an already-placed instance, repeating a no-change navigation, or trying yet another receptacle after many failed put attempts can exhaust the action budget and cause failure. A held object whose put attempts fail across many receptacles may indicate an unplaceable object or an infeasible goal rather than a wrong receptacle.
why_it_happens: Searching without tracking checked locations and placed instances leads to redundant actions, while unchecked opened containers or visible surfaces may still contain the target. A no-change navigation indicates the target location is unreachable or invalid, so retrying it cannot help.
how_to_avoid: Maintain a list of checked locations and placed instances. Prioritize unchecked opened containers and visible surfaces; take a target directly if it is visible. Avoid revisiting a location confirmed to have no target or re-taking an already-placed object unless new evidence suggests otherwise. After one no-change navigation, choose a different unchecked location. If every put attempt fails across many receptacles, stop suggesting new receptacles and reassess the held object's exact identifier and whether the destination accepts placement, considering the object unplaceable or the goal infeasible.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_009 | Failure Lesson]
description: Repeatedly declaring a subtask complete without executing the required next action can trigger a loop guard and terminate the episode before the two items are placed. Re-taking an already-placed item and re-placing it at a different instance of the destination can also trigger a guard.
why_it_happens: The current state may be misread as satisfying the completion condition even though the actual goal or subgoal is unfinished, causing repeated signals instead of progress; alternatively, the destination instance may be confused, leading to re-taking a placed item.
how_to_avoid: Signal completion only after the corresponding subgoal is actually achieved, such as an object being taken or placed. After signaling, continue with the necessary next action and avoid repeating the same completion signal without new progress. Track which destination instance is the goal; once an item is placed at the target, do not re-take it—search for a second instance instead.

For each cycle: locate and take one target object, navigate to the destination, open it if closed, place the object, and verify the placement from the observation before starting the next cycle. Track how many items are placed and which item was already placed; never take an already-placed item again. If a second take fails while an object is held, place the held object at the destination before returning for the second. If both instances are visible on the same surface or receptacle, place the first and then return to that same location for the second. If the final destination is temporarily unavailable, use only a safe recoverable holding location when necessary, then move both objects to the final destination afterward. Treat each placement as a checkpoint, not task completion.
when_to_apply: When the goal requires placing two instances of the same object type at one target location and only one object can be carried at a time.

title: Systematic broad search with checked-location tracking
principle: When target objects are not immediately visible, search broadly rather than checking only one receptacle type. Inspect visible open surfaces such as counters, tables, shelves, sofas, and similar surfaces first, then check closed containers such as cabinets and drawers, opening them before inspecting or taking from inside. Continue across multiple location types until the required number of instances is found or a checked-location record shows no remaining unchecked likely locations. If both target instances are visible on the same surface, take one, place it, then return to that same surface for the second rather than wandering to unrelated containers. Treat an unreachable or no-change navigation target as unavailable and move to another candidate. Reassess feasibility after likely locations are exhausted, but do not conclude the task is blocked prematurely.
when_to_apply: When one or both target objects are not visible and must be located in the environment.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_003 | Failure Lesson]
description: Attempts to take a second object, or sometimes to move to another location, while already holding an object can return no effect. This blocks progress in two-item placement if the held object is not released first. A failed second take while an object is held should be diagnosed as the one-item carry limit, not as the second object being absent.
why_it_happens: The environment commonly allows carrying only one object at a time, so take or movement actions may be rejected while inventory is occupied.
how_to_avoid: Before taking the second object or moving to search elsewhere, put the held object into the final destination or into a safe recoverable temporary location. Confirm the hands are empty, then continue. When a take fails while holding an object, attribute it to occupied inventory and place the held object first rather than concluding the target is missing.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_004 | Failure Lesson]
description: A put action can produce no effect if issued before reaching the destination receptacle, or it can fail without the failure being noticed. title: Search observable surfaces first, then broaden to closed containers
principle: When the target object's location is unknown, locate it before manipulation by checking open, directly observable surfaces and common holding places first: tables, countertops, desks, dressers, shelves, beds, sofas, chairs, and other plausible visible surfaces such as toilets or TV stands when they could hold the target. Only then open closed containers such as drawers, cabinets, fridges, microwaves, and similar receptacles. Treat search as a broad multi-location search rather than assuming one named receptacle contains the object. If an early location is empty, broaden to other plausible unchecked locations. If the target or a required fixture is already visible on a surface, go directly to that furniture instead of continuing unrelated container checks.
when_to_apply: When the target object's location is unknown at the start, when the first checked location does not contain it, or when the target or a required fixture is already visible on a surface.
[General | G_002 | Failure Lesson]
description: Failed searches often repeat the same empty surfaces or failed take attempts, revisit already-confirmed-empty locations, or conclude the object is unavailable before all plausible open surfaces and relevant containers have been checked. A search should maintain a checked-location list and move to a new unchecked plausible location after a failed take or empty look.
why_it_happens: Search may be treated as an unconstrained sequence without bookkeeping, so empty locations are revisited and some plausible locations are never examined; alternatively, failure may be declared after only a subset of locations is checked.
how_to_avoid: Record each checked location and its result. After a failed take or empty look, mark that location checked and move to another plausible unchecked location. title: Open closed containers before taking or placing and verify destination openability

when_to_apply: When the target may be inside a closed container, or when the placement destination is closed or its openability is uncertain.

[General | G_001 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Search observable surfaces first, then broaden to closed containers
principle: When the target object's location is unknown, locate it before manipulation by checking open, directly observable surfaces and common holding places first: tables, countertops, desks, dressers, shelves, beds, sofas, chairs, and other plausible visible surfaces such as toilets or TV stands when they could hold the target. Only then open closed containers such as drawers, cabinets, fridges, microwaves, and similar receptacles. Treat search as a broad multi-location search rather than assuming one named receptacle contains the object. If an early location is empty, broaden to other plausible unchecked locations. If the target or a required fixture is already visible on a surface, go directly to that furniture instead of continuing unrelated container checks.
when_to_apply: When the target object's location is unknown at the start, when the first checked location does not contain it, or when the target or a required fixture is already visible on a surface.
[General | G_002 | Failure Lesson]
description: Failed searches often repeat the same empty surfaces or failed take attempts, revisit already-confirmed-empty locations, or conclude the object is unavailable before all plausible open surfaces and relevant containers have been checked. A search should maintain a checked-location list and move to a new unchecked plausible location after a failed take or empty look.
why_it_happens: Search may be treated as an unconstrained sequence without bookkeeping, so empty locations are revisited and some plausible locations are never examined; alternatively, failure may be declared after only a subset of locations is checked.
how_to_avoid: Record each checked location and its result. After a failed take or empty look, mark that location checked and move to another plausible unchecked location. Do not revisit confirmed empty surfaces unless the environment state changed. Open closed receptacles before treating them as searched and prioritize locations by object type. If the object remains absent after relevant locations are exhausted, report failure rather than continuing indefinitely; but do not declare blocked while plausible unchecked locations remain.

title: Open closed containers before taking or placing and verify destination openability
principle: When a closed drawer, cabinet, safe, fridge, microwave, or similar container may hold the target or is the placement destination, navigate to it and open it before attempting to take from it or put into it. when_to_apply: When the target may be inside a closed container, or when the placement destination is closed or its openability is uncertain.

title: Position at the object's receptacle before take and at the destination before put

Once the target is held, travel directly to the specified destination and place it without unnecessary intermediate steps; if a put fails, verify current location and navigate to the destination before retrying.
when_to_apply: When retrieving an object whose location is not current, when moving a held object to a destination, or after a failed put.
[General | G_005 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Use supported action forms, exact identifiers, and matching object instances
principle: Use only supported action forms: go to a location, take an object from a receptacle, put an object in or on a receptacle, open a container before accessing it, and use a fixture with its numbered instance when applicable. when_to_apply: Throughout object search, retrieval, and placement, especially when forming commands or when an action seems unsupported or ambiguous.
[General | G_006 | Failure Lesson]
description: When an action such as go to, open, take, put, use, or clean returns no change, do not repeat the same command. Failed attempts can come from being at the wrong location, using an inexact or invalid identifier, targeting a closed or non-openable receptacle, or trying an inaccessible location. Treat an unreachable navigation target as unavailable and switch to another candidate; treat an already-open container as open and continue rather than reopening it. Repeated no-change results are evidence that the current approach is exhausted.
why_it_happens: The same invalid action may be retried without updating the inferred state, and a failed task segment may be reissued identically instead of changing the search location, object description, or strategy.
how_to_avoid: After a no-change observation, re-check location, inventory, exact identifiers, and object or container state. Change at least one relevant condition: move to a different reachable location, open a closed container, use the specific instance id, or switch to another strategy. After one or two identical failures, stop retrying. If a task segment fails or returns without meeting its condition, do not repeat it unchanged; broaden the search or change the approach. Before declaring blocked, ensure every plausible closed container was actually opened and inspected, not merely approached, and avoid revisiting surfaces already confirmed empty.

title: Separate acquisition from operation with observable completion conditions
principle: For tasks that require an object to be found and then manipulated, cleaned, heated, cooled, examined, or placed, split the task into an acquisition phase and an operation phase. The operation phase ends only when the environment observation confirms the required final state, such as the object being at the destination, cleaned, heated, or cooled. why_it_happens: Placement requires being at the target container, and a successful put must be verified from the observation; otherwise the first item may still be held or not placed. how_to_avoid: Navigate to the destination before placing. After each put, inspect the observation to confirm success. Issuing open on a container while standing at its parent furniture may return no change; the actor must navigate to the container itself first.
why_it_happens: The environment requires the container to be open before its contents can be accessed or modified, reports no change when opening an already-open container, and validates open actions against the actor's current location being the container rather than its parent furniture.
how_to_avoid: Navigate to the container itself, then open it with the appropriate open action. If it is already open, or if opening returns no change, proceed to take or place rather than retrying open. After opening, verify access before taking or placing. Do not issue open on a container from its parent furniture.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_006 | Failure Lesson]
description: Using an examine-style action on objects or locations is not supported and returns no useful information.
why_it_happens: The available interaction set is limited to navigation, taking, putting, opening, and inventory-style operations; examining is not an effective substitute.
how_to_avoid: Inspect a location by navigating to the receptacle and observing its contents. Pick up visible target objects with a take action from that receptacle.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_007 | Failure Lesson]
description: Placing an object into a non-target or unsuitable container such as a garbage can can make retrieval impossible or cause the overall two-item placement to fail.
why_it_happens: Some containers may not accept objects cleanly, may change object state, or may not allow reliable retrieval; temporary storage is only safe if the object can be taken back.
how_to_avoid: Prefer placing the first object directly into the final destination. If temporary holding is unavoidable, choose an open, stable, recoverable surface or container and avoid garbage cans or other likely irreversible containers.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_008 | Failure Lesson]
description: After several containers have been opened and no target found, repeatedly revisiting locations already confirmed empty, re-taking an already-placed instance, repeating a no-change navigation, or trying yet another receptacle after many failed put attempts can exhaust the action budget and cause failure. A held object whose put attempts fail across many receptacles may indicate an unplaceable object or an infeasible goal rather than a wrong receptacle.
why_it_happens: Searching without tracking checked locations and placed instances leads to redundant actions, while unchecked opened containers or visible surfaces may still contain the target. A no-change navigation indicates the target location is unreachable or invalid, so retrying it cannot help.
how_to_avoid: Maintain a list of checked locations and placed instances. Prioritize unchecked opened containers and visible surfaces; take a target directly if it is visible. Avoid revisiting a location confirmed to have no target or re-taking an already-placed object unless new evidence suggests otherwise. After one no-change navigation, choose a different unchecked location. If every put attempt fails across many receptacles, stop suggesting new receptacles and reassess the held object's exact identifier and whether the destination accepts placement, considering the object unplaceable or the goal infeasible.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_009 | Failure Lesson]
description: Repeatedly declaring a subtask complete without executing the required next action can trigger a loop guard and terminate the episode before the two items are placed. Re-taking an already-placed item and re-placing it at a different instance of the destination can also trigger a guard.
why_it_happens: The current state may be misread as satisfying the completion condition even though the actual goal or subgoal is unfinished, causing repeated signals instead of progress; alternatively, the destination instance may be confused, leading to re-taking a placed item.
how_to_avoid: Signal completion only after the corresponding subgoal is actually achieved, such as an object being taken or placed. After signaling, continue with the necessary next action and avoid repeating the same completion signal without new progress. Track which destination instance is the goal; once an item is placed at the target, do not re-take it—search for a second instance instead.

why_it_happens: Search may be treated as an unconstrained sequence without bookkeeping, so empty locations are revisited and some plausible locations are never examined; alternatively, failure may be declared after only a subset of locations is checked.
how_to_avoid: Record each checked location and its result. After a failed take or empty look, mark that location checked and move to another plausible unchecked location. If the object remains absent after relevant locations are exhausted, report failure rather than continuing indefinitely; but do not declare blocked while plausible unchecked locations remain.
[General | G_003 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Open closed containers before taking or placing and verify destination openability
principle: When a closed drawer, cabinet, safe, fridge, microwave, or similar container may hold the target or is the placement destination, navigate to it and open it before attempting to take from it or put into it. Closed containers cannot be inspected or used directly. Before placing, confirm the destination is already open or can be opened; if opening returns no change, treat it as non-openable and choose a valid open destination or surface. For non-openable fixtures, use only a go-then-put sequence.
when_to_apply: When the target may be inside a closed container, or when the placement destination is closed or its openability is uncertain.
[General | G_004 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Position at the object's receptacle before take and at the destination before put
principle: A take action succeeds only when the actor is at the receptacle where the object is present, and a put action succeeds only when the actor is at the destination. When retrieving, first locate the object and position at its receptacle before taking. Once the target is held, travel directly to the specified destination and place it without unnecessary intermediate steps; if a put fails, verify current location and navigate to the destination before retrying.
when_to_apply: When retrieving an object whose location is not current, when moving a held object to a destination, or after a failed put.
[General | G_005 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Use supported action forms, exact identifiers, and matching object instances
principle: Use only supported action forms: go to a location, take an object from a receptacle, put an object in or on a receptacle, open a container before accessing it, and use a fixture with its numbered instance when applicable. Refer to exact object and receptacle identifiers from observations, including instance numbers, and track the specific instance taken so later actions use the same one. Prefer navigating to locations, furniture, or receptacles rather than to a takeable object when the action form requires it. Do not use examine, look at, or open on non-container surfaces; open only applies to openable containers. Before taking or transforming, confirm the object name matches the goal, because similar types may not satisfy it. If many containers have been checked without success, reassess visible surfaces and the target description rather than continuing blind exhaustive checks.
when_to_apply: Throughout object search, retrieval, and placement, especially when forming commands or when an action seems unsupported or ambiguous.
[General | G_006 | Failure Lesson]
description: When an action such as go to, open, take, put, use, or clean returns no change, do not repeat the same command. Failed attempts can come from being at the wrong location, using an inexact or invalid identifier, targeting a closed or non-openable receptacle, or trying an inaccessible location. Treat an unreachable navigation target as unavailable and switch to another candidate; treat an already-open container as open and continue rather than reopening it. Repeated no-change results are evidence that the current approach is exhausted.
why_it_happens: The same invalid action may be retried without updating the inferred state, and a failed task segment may be reissued identically instead of changing the search location, object description, or strategy.
how_to_avoid: After a no-change observation, re-check location, inventory, exact identifiers, and object or container state. Change at least one relevant condition: move to a different reachable location, open a closed container, use the specific instance id, or switch to another strategy. [General | G_007 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Separate acquisition from operation with observable completion conditions
principle: For tasks that require an object to be found and then manipulated, cleaned, heated, cooled, examined, or placed, split the task into an acquisition phase and an operation phase. The acquisition phase ends only when the target object is actually held, not merely seen and not merely because a container was opened. The operation phase ends only when the environment observation confirms the required final state, such as the object being at the destination, cleaned, heated, or cooled. Begin placement only after acquisition is confirmed by holding the target object. If a subsequent phase or handoff follows, report acquisition only after the take observation confirms holding and note any remaining operation.
when_to_apply: When a goal requires an object to be acquired before it is used, transformed, or placed, and the object is not already held.
[General | G_008 | Failure Lesson]
description: Do not declare completion or stop based on an attempted action alone. After critical actions such as take, put, clean, heat, or cool, inspect the observation for the goal predicate. how_to_avoid: After each critical action, compare the observation with the expected state. If the action failed, retry only after adjusting the approach; if it succeeded, stop issuing extra actions. Do not declare completion before the final placement is confirmed; after confirmation, stop and do not send empty or inventory-only actions.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_001 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Two-item sequential placement with per-item verification and placed-item tracking
principle: Treat a two-item placement goal as two search-and-place cycles. If a second take fails while an object is held, place the held object at the destination before returning for the second. If both instances are visible on the same surface or receptacle, place the first and then return to that same location for the second. If the final destination is temporarily unavailable, use only a safe recoverable holding location when necessary, then move both objects to the final destination afterward. when_to_apply: When the goal requires placing two instances of the same object type at one target location and only one object can be carried at a time.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_002 | Procedure or Local Strategy]
title: Systematic broad search with checked-location tracking

when_to_apply: When one or both target objects are not visible and must be located in the environment.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_003 | Failure Lesson]
description: Attempts to take a second object, or sometimes to move to another location, while already holding an object can return no effect. why_it_happens: The environment commonly allows carrying only one object at a time, so take or movement actions may be rejected while inventory is occupied.
how_to_avoid: Before taking the second object or moving to search elsewhere, put the held object into the final destination or into a safe recoverable temporary location. [Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_004 | Failure Lesson]
description: A put action can produce no effect if issued before reaching the destination receptacle, or it can fail without the failure being noticed. [Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_005 | Failure Lesson]
description: Attempting to put an object into, or take an object from, a closed cabinet, drawer, or similar container may produce no effect. Issuing open on a container while standing at its parent furniture may return no change; the actor must navigate to the container itself first.

how_to_avoid: Navigate to the container itself, then open it with the appropriate open action. If it is already open, or if opening returns no change, proceed to take or place rather than retrying open. After opening, verify access before taking or placing. Do not issue open on a container from its parent furniture.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_006 | Failure Lesson]
description: Using an examine-style action on objects or locations is not supported and returns no useful information.
why_it_happens: The available interaction set is limited to navigation, taking, putting, opening, and inventory-style operations; examining is not an effective substitute.
how_to_avoid: Inspect a location by navigating to the receptacle and observing its contents. Pick up visible target objects with a take action from that receptacle.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_007 | Failure Lesson]
description: Placing an object into a non-target or unsuitable container such as a garbage can can make retrieval impossible or cause the overall two-item placement to fail.
why_it_happens: Some containers may not accept objects cleanly, may change object state, or may not allow reliable retrieval; temporary storage is only safe if the object can be taken back.
how_to_avoid: Prefer placing the first object directly into the final destination. If temporary holding is unavoidable, choose an open, stable, recoverable surface or container and avoid garbage cans or other likely irreversible containers.
[Task-specific: 双物品放置 | T6_008 | Failure Lesson]
description: After several containers have been opened and no target found, repeatedly revisiting locations already confirmed empty, re-taking an already-placed instance, repeating a no-change navigation, or trying yet another receptacle after many failed put attempts can exhaust the action budget and cause failure. why_it_happens: Searching without tracking checked locations and placed instances leads to redundant actions, while unchecked opened containers or visible surfaces may still contain the target.
